# Purpose

Step 2 of the clean donor-level pseudobulk analysis. Picks up the 806
QC-passing libraries from step 1 and:

1. loads the MiXCR BCR calls and counts heavy and light chains,
2. builds **Supplemental Figures S5B and S5C**,
3. removes doublets,
4. assigns each cell an IgH isotype from its heavy chain, the input to
   **main text Figure 5A** (drawn by `figure_panels/Fig5A_isotype_frequencies.R`),
5. calls clonal expansion following the published methods and builds
   **Supplemental Figure S5D**, and
6. computes repertoire diversity metrics answering **reviewer comment 8**.

Every figure panel gets a source-data table saved alongside it (JCI Insight
requires per-panel source data).

Scope: BCR chain analysis and the figures that depend on it. Draw-to-processing
time, normalization and the cell-level PCA/UMAP are in step 3; pseudobulk
differential expression is in step 4. Raw counts pass through untouched.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(shazam)    # distToNearest / findThreshold (Immcantation)
library(alakazam)  # alphaDiversity (Immcantation)
library(stringdist)
```

# Parameters

```{r params}
## --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
## All pipeline inputs live in inputs/ (see inputs/README.md for provenance).
INPUT_DIR   <- "inputs"
MIXCR_CSV   <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "Mixcr_summary_updated_with_Nucleotidesequences_1stAug2025_PseudogeneFiltered.csv")
EXCLUDE_CSV <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "QC_libids_HCLC_tobeExcluded_Aug2025.csv")

STEP1_RDS    <- file.path("pseudobulk_clean_output", "step1_counts_qc.rds")
STEP1_QC_CSV <- file.path("pseudobulk_clean_output", "step1_library_qc_metrics.csv")
OUT_DIR      <- "pseudobulk_clean_output"
FIG_DIR      <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures")
SRC_DIR      <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "figure_source_data")   # JCI source-data tables

## --- Doublet definition ------------------------------------------------------
MIN_HEAVY_DOUBLET <- 2   # >= this many heavy chains => doublet
MIN_LIGHT_DOUBLET <- 3   # >= this many light chains => doublet

## --- Clonal expansion (Supplemental Figure S5D) ------------------------------
## Follows the published methods: per donor and chain type, nearest-neighbour
## distances between CDR3 nucleotide sequences via shazam::distToNearest
## (Hamming, length-normalized, grouped by V/J gene and junction length), then
## "Expanded" = EITHER
##   (i)  nearest-neighbour distance < CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD, OR
##   (ii) identical V gene, J gene, C gene and CDR3 nucleotide sequence shared
##        by at least CLONE_MIN_SIZE cells in that donor.
CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD <- 0.193   # the published threshold
CLONE_MIN_SIZE       <- 2

## Which chain type decides whether a CELL is expanded. Clonality is defined by
## the heavy chain: light-chain CDR3s are short and convergent, so unrelated
## cells routinely share one (see the sensitivity table below).
CLONE_CHAINS           <- "heavy"
CLONE_IDENTICAL_CHAINS <- "heavy"   # scope of criterion (ii)

## Denominator for the per-donor proportion.
##   "assessed"  : cells carrying a chain of the relevant type (default; a cell
##                 with no heavy chain cannot be called either way)
##   "all_cells" : all 801 cells, counting unassessable cells as not expanded
CLONE_DENOMINATOR <- "assessed"

## Report what findThreshold() derives from these data next to the 0.193 used in
## the methods. Informational only; CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD is what gets applied.
REPORT_FINDTHRESHOLD <- TRUE

## --- Repertoire metrics (reviewer comment 8) ---------------------------------
DIVERSITY_NBOOT <- 200   # bootstrap replicates for alakazam::alphaDiversity
RAREFY_REPS     <- 200   # resampling replicates for rarefied metrics

## The metrics reported in both the statistics table and the figure. Depth-driven
## metrics (raw Shannon, Hill numbers, group counts) are computed for reference
## but not reported, because they correlate with cells sequenced at r ~ 1.
REPORT_METRICS <- c("rarefiedRichness", "rarefiedHill1", "evenness",
                    "pctCellsInExpandedGroups", "top1Share", "vGeneShannon")

SEED <- 42

## --- Manuscript figure panels ------------------------------------------------
GROUP_COLORS <- c(TC = "blue", DS = "red")   # as published

## Which libraries feed BOTH Supplemental Figure S5B and S5C. One shared
## parameter on purpose: the two panels describe the same cells, so they are
## drawn on the same set.
##   "qc_passing"    : the 806 libraries passing step 1 QC (default; upstream of
##                     the doublet cut, so the doublets are visible in panel C)
##   "post_doublet"  : the 801 analysis cells
##   "all_libraries" : all 864 sequenced libraries
S5_LIBRARY_SET <- "qc_passing"

set.seed(SEED)
for (d in c(OUT_DIR, FIG_DIR, SRC_DIR)) dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Load step 1

```{r load_step1}
step1     <- readRDS(STEP1_RDS)
rawCounts <- step1$counts        # raw integer counts, genes x libraries
libAnno   <- step1$libAnno       # one row per QC-passing library
geneAnno  <- step1$geneAnno

cat(sprintf("step 1: %d genes x %d QC-passing libraries\n",
            nrow(rawCounts), ncol(rawCounts)))
```

# BCR calls and chain counts

MiXCR rows are one chain per row. Two filters are applied before counting:
the prior analyst's manual exclusion list (matched on `libid` +
`full_nt_sequence`), and dropping any chain that is neither heavy (IGH) nor
light (IGK/IGL).

```{r load_bcrs}
bcrsRaw <- read_csv(MIXCR_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE)
exclude <- read_csv(EXCLUDE_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal") %>%
  dplyr::select(libid, full_nt_sequence) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(libid))

## Classified but NOT yet restricted to QC-passing libraries, so that
## S5_LIBRARY_SET can select any of the three library sets below.
bcrsClassified <- bcrsRaw %>%
  dplyr::anti_join(exclude, by = c("libid", "full_nt_sequence")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chain = dplyr::case_when(
    str_detect(v_gene, "IGH")      ~ "heavy",
    str_detect(v_gene, "IGK|IGL")  ~ "light",
    TRUE                           ~ "other")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(chain != "other")

bcrs <- bcrsClassified %>% dplyr::filter(libid %in% libAnno$libid)

cat(sprintf("MiXCR rows: %d -> %d after exclusion list, chain filter, and QC libraries\n",
            nrow(bcrsRaw), nrow(bcrs)))
```

```{r chain_counts}
chainCounts <- bcrs %>%
  dplyr::count(libid, chain) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = chain, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

libAnno <- libAnno %>%
  dplyr::left_join(chainCounts, by = "libid") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    numheavy = tidyr::replace_na(heavy, 0),
    numlight = tidyr::replace_na(light, 0),
    bcrGroup = dplyr::case_when(numheavy > 0 & numlight > 0 ~ "both",
                                numheavy > 0                ~ "heavy only",
                                numlight > 0                ~ "light only",
                                TRUE                        ~ "no bcr"),
    is_doublet = numheavy >= MIN_HEAVY_DOUBLET | numlight >= MIN_LIGHT_DOUBLET) %>%
  dplyr::select(-heavy, -light)

kable(libAnno %>% dplyr::count(numheavy, numlight, is_doublet),
      caption = "Heavy / light chain counts per library")
kable(libAnno %>% dplyr::count(bcrGroup, name = "nLibraries"),
      caption = "BCR recovery")

cat(sprintf("\nflagged as doublets: %d | would remain after removal: %d\n",
            sum(libAnno$is_doublet), sum(!libAnno$is_doublet)))
```

The doublet cut is applied further down, *after* the supplemental panels, so
those panels can show the chain-recovery distribution that motivates it.

# Manuscript figure panels

Repeating the upstream supplemental panels from this pipeline, with a source-data
table saved alongside each one (JCI Insight requires per-panel source data).

Both panels are drawn on the **same** library set (`S5_LIBRARY_SET`, default the
806 libraries passing step 1 QC) and sit **upstream of the doublet cut**. That
ordering is deliberate: panel C's whole point is the chain-recovery
distribution, and the cells carrying two or more heavy chains are exactly the
ones the doublet rule removes, so drawing it after removal would delete the
evidence for the cut. Panel B on the same set then describes the same cells.

Neither panel depends on the isotype-call correction above --- both count cells
and chains, not isotypes --- so they are a clean end-to-end check on the
pipeline before we rely on it for anything new.

```{r fig_helpers}
## All 864 sequenced libraries with their QC verdict, from step 1.
allLibs <- read_csv(STEP1_QC_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::select(libid, donorId, project, studyGroup, qcPass) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(studyGroup = factor(studyGroup, levels = c("TC", "DS")))

## Donors ordered by group, then numerically within group.
donorLevels <- allLibs %>%
  dplyr::distinct(project, studyGroup) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(num = as.numeric(str_remove(project, "P635-"))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(studyGroup, num) %>%
  dplyr::pull(project)

saveSource <- function(dat, panel, description) {
  path <- file.path(SRC_DIR, sprintf("%s.csv", panel))
  write_csv(dat, path)
  cat(sprintf("source data: %-42s %4d rows  (%s)\n", basename(path), nrow(dat), description))
  invisible(path)
}
savePanel <- function(plot, panel, width = 6.5, height = 4) {
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s.pdf", panel)), plot, width = width, height = height)
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s.png", panel)), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  invisible(plot)
}
```

```{r fig_library_set}
s5Libs <- switch(S5_LIBRARY_SET,

cat(sprintf("panels S5B and S5C both drawn on %d libraries (%s)\n",
```

## Supplemental Figure S5B --- cells sequenced per donor

```{r fig_S5B, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4}
s5b <- s5Libs %>%

  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

print(pS5B)

kable(s5b, caption = "Source data, Supplemental Figure S5B")
cat(sprintf("total cells: %d\n", sum(s5b$nCells)))
```

## Supplemental Figure S5C --- heavy and light chains recovered per cell

Chain counts per cell. With the default library set this is before doublet
removal, so the cells with two or more heavy chains --- the ones the doublet rule
removes --- are visible here.

```{r fig_S5C, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.8}
s5cCounts <- bcrsClassified %>%
  dplyr::filter(libid %in% s5Libs$libid) %>%
  dplyr::count(libid, chain) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = chain, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

s5c <- s5Libs %>%
  dplyr::left_join(s5cCounts, by = "libid") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(numheavy = tidyr::replace_na(heavy, 0),
                numlight = tidyr::replace_na(light, 0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(libid, donorId, project, studyGroup, numheavy, numlight)

pS5C <- ggplot(s5c, aes(numlight, numheavy, colour = studyGroup)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ studyGroup) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:max(s5c$numlight)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:max(s5c$numheavy)) +
  labs(x = "# light chains", y = "# heavy chains",
       title = "Supplemental Figure S5C: chains recovered per cell",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s (n = %d libraries)", S5_LIBRARY_SET, nrow(s5c))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
print(pS5C)

```

```{r fig_S5C_tables}
## Exact counts behind the jitter, which the plot itself cannot convey.
s5cCrossTab <- s5c %>%
  dplyr::count(studyGroup, numheavy, numlight, name = "nCells") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(studyGroup, numheavy, numlight)
kable(s5cCrossTab %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = numlight, values_from = nCells, values_fill = 0,
                           names_prefix = "light_"),
      caption = "Cells per heavy x light chain combination")

## Per-donor chain totals.
s5cPerDonor <- s5c %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyGroup, project, donorId) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nCells = dplyr::n(), heavyChains = sum(numheavy),
                   lightChains = sum(numlight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(project = factor(project, levels = donorLevels)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(project)
kable(s5cPerDonor, caption = "Source data, Supplemental Figure S5C (per-donor totals)")
```

# Doublet removal

With the supplemental panels drawn, apply the cut. Everything downstream --- the
isotype assignment, the embeddings, and the pseudobulk in step 3 --- uses this
set.

```{r remove_doublets}
cells <- libAnno %>% dplyr::filter(!is_doublet)
cat(sprintf("doublets removed: %d | cells retained: %d\n",
            sum(libAnno$is_doublet), nrow(cells)))
kable(libAnno %>% dplyr::filter(is_doublet) %>%
        dplyr::select(libid, donorId, project, studyGroup, numheavy, numlight),
      caption = "Libraries removed as doublets")
```

# Isotype assignment

A cell carries at most one heavy chain after doublet removal, so the IgH isotype
is read directly off it. Cells with light chains only get `NA` --- they have no
IgH isotype to assign.

```{r assign_isotype}
cells <- cells %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    bcrs %>%
      dplyr::filter(libid %in% cells$libid, chain == "heavy") %>%
      dplyr::group_by(libid) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::transmute(libid, isotype = str_extract(c_gene, "^IGH[ADGME]")),
    by = "libid")

kable(cells %>% dplyr::count(isotype, name = "nCells") %>% dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(nCells)),
      caption = "Isotype distribution")
kable(cells %>% dplyr::count(studyGroup, isotype) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = studyGroup, values_from = n, values_fill = 0),
      caption = "Isotype by study group")
nHeavy <- dplyr::n_distinct(bcrs$libid[bcrs$chain == "heavy" & bcrs$libid %in% cells$libid])
cat(sprintf("cells with an assigned isotype: %d of %d\n", sum(!is.na(cells$isotype)), nrow(cells)))
cat(sprintf("cells carrying a heavy chain:   %d (the difference had a heavy chain with no parseable C gene)\n",
            nHeavy))
```

# Main text Figure 5A --- isotype frequencies per donor

The panel and its JCI Insight source-data tables are built by
`figure_panels/Fig5A_isotype_frequencies.R`, which reads the
`step2_cell_metadata.csv` written below. Keeping the drawing out of this
notebook means one script owns each panel's files; run it after this notebook:

```
Rscript figure_panels/Fig5A_isotype_frequencies.R
```

That script computes, per donor, the percentage of isotype-assignable cells
carrying each IgH isotype. Cells with no heavy chain, or a heavy chain with no
parseable C gene, are excluded from numerator and denominator alike, and the
per-donor denominator is written to the source table so any percentage can be
recomputed. It asserts that each donor's four percentages sum to 100 --- the
four plotted isotypes are the only ones called in these data, so anything else
means the numerators and the denominator came from different cell sets.

The four percentages are compositional, so the four tests are not independent.
The script reports the raw p-values from both a Welch t-test and a Wilcoxon
rank-sum test for every isotype, and can additionally apply Benjamini-Hochberg
across the four isotypes of the panel (valid here under positive dependence).

# Supplemental Figure S5D --- clonal expansion

Drawn on the **801-cell** post-doublet set, since a doublet would create a
spurious pairing.

This follows the published methods: nearest-neighbour CDR3 nucleotide distances
per donor and chain type (`shazam::distToNearest`, Hamming model,
length-normalized, grouped by V/J gene and junction length), then two
complementary criteria for calling a sequence expanded --- a nearest neighbour
closer than the distance threshold, or an identical V/J/C/CDR3-nt sequence
shared with another cell in the same donor.

## One sequence per cell per chain

```{r clone_sequences}
## distToNearest finds each sequence's nearest neighbour within its group. If a
## cell contributed two chain rows, the cell would be its own neighbour, so
## reduce to one sequence per cell per chain type first.
cloneSeqs <- bcrs %>%
  dplyr::filter(libid %in% cells$libid, !is.na(cdr3_nt_sequence), cdr3_nt_sequence != "") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(libid, chain) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cells %>% dplyr::select(libid, donorId, project, studyGroup, isotype),
                   by = "libid") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(sequence_id = paste0(libid, "_", chain), libid, donorId, project,
                   studyGroup, isotype, chain,
                   locus  = str_sub(v_gene, 1, 3),
                   v_call = v_gene, j_call = j_gene, c_call = c_gene,
                   ## amino-acid CDR3 kept for readable tables; `junction` is
                   ## the nucleotide sequence the distance model operates on
                   cdr3_aa = junction,
                   junction = cdr3_nt_sequence)

cat(sprintf("sequences: %d (heavy %d, light %d) from %d cells\n",
            nrow(cloneSeqs), sum(cloneSeqs$chain == "heavy"),
            sum(cloneSeqs$chain == "light"), dplyr::n_distinct(cloneSeqs$libid)))
```

## Nearest-neighbour distances

```{r clone_distances}
## Computed separately for each donor and chain type, as in the methods.
cloneDist <- cloneSeqs %>%
  dplyr::group_split(project, chain) %>%
  lapply(function(d) {
    if (nrow(d) < 2) { d$dist_nearest <- NA_real_; return(d) }
    suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(tryCatch(
      distToNearest(as.data.frame(d), sequenceColumn = "junction",
                    vCallColumn = "v_call", jCallColumn = "j_call",
                    model = "ham", normalize = "len", nproc = 1,
                    locusColumn = "locus", locusValues = unique(d$locus),
                    onlyHeavy = FALSE, keepVJLgroup = FALSE),
      error = function(e) { d$dist_nearest <- NA_real_; d })))
  }) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows()

cat(sprintf("distances computed for %d of %d sequences (a sequence needs another with the same V, J and junction length in that donor)\n",
            sum(!is.na(cloneDist$dist_nearest)), nrow(cloneDist)))

if (REPORT_FINDTHRESHOLD) {
  for (m in c("density", "gmm")) {
    th <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
      findThreshold(cloneDist$dist_nearest[!is.na(cloneDist$dist_nearest)], method = m),
      error = function(e) NULL))
    cat(sprintf("findThreshold(%-7s) on these data: %s | applied threshold: %.3f\n", m,
                if (!is.null(th) && !is.na(th@threshold)) sprintf("%.3f", th@threshold) else "not returned",
                CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD))
  }
}

ggplot(cloneDist %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(dist_nearest)),
       aes(dist_nearest, fill = chain)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "nearest-neighbour CDR3 nt distance (length-normalized Hamming)",
       y = "sequences", fill = NULL,
       title = "Nearest-neighbour distance distribution",
       subtitle = sprintf("dashed line = applied threshold %.3f", CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

## Applying the two criteria

```{r clone_criteria}
callExpansion <- function(dist_threshold = CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD,
                          chains = CLONE_CHAINS, minSize = CLONE_MIN_SIZE,
                          requireCDR3 = TRUE, denominator = CLONE_DENOMINATOR,
                          identicalChains = CLONE_IDENTICAL_CHAINS) {
  key <- if (requireCDR3) c("v_call", "j_call", "c_call", "junction") else
                          c("v_call", "j_call", "c_call")
  seqLevel <- cloneDist %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c("project", key)))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(nCellsIdentical = dplyr::n_distinct(libid)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(critDistance  = !is.na(dist_nearest) & dist_nearest < dist_threshold,
                  critIdentical = nCellsIdentical >= minSize,
                  expandedSeq   = critDistance | critIdentical)
  ## The two criteria are scoped independently, so a cell can qualify by a
  ## heavy-chain distance match or by an identical sequence on either chain.
  inScope <- function(scope) if (scope == "heavy") seqLevel$chain == "heavy" else
                             rep(TRUE, nrow(seqLevel))
  distScope  <- inScope(chains)
  identScope <- inScope(identicalChains)
  cellLevel <- seqLevel %>%
    dplyr::mutate(hitDistance  = critDistance  & distScope,
                  hitIdentical = critIdentical & identScope) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(libid) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(byDistance  = any(hitDistance),
                     byIdentical = any(hitIdentical),
                     expanded    = any(hitDistance) | any(hitIdentical),
                     .groups = "drop")
  ## "assessed" = cells carrying a chain of the type the distance criterion uses.
  assessable <- unique(seqLevel$libid[distScope])
  out <- if (denominator == "all_cells") {
    cells %>% dplyr::left_join(cellLevel, by = "libid") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(byDistance, byIdentical, expanded),
                                  ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, FALSE)))
  } else {
    cells %>% dplyr::filter(libid %in% assessable) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(cellLevel, by = "libid") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(byDistance, byIdentical, expanded),
                                  ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, FALSE)))
  }
  list(seqLevel = seqLevel, cells = out)
}

expansion <- callExpansion()
seqLevel  <- expansion$seqLevel
cellExp   <- expansion$cells

cat(sprintf("criterion (i) distance < %.3f: %d sequences | criterion (ii) identical V/J/C/CDR3: %d | either: %d\n",
            CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD, sum(seqLevel$critDistance), sum(seqLevel$critIdentical),
            sum(seqLevel$expandedSeq)))
cat(sprintf("cells assessed (%s chain): %d of %d | expanded: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            CLONE_CHAINS, nrow(cellExp), nrow(cells), sum(cellExp$expanded),
            100 * mean(cellExp$expanded)))
cat(sprintf("  by distance criterion: %d | by identity criterion (%s chain): %d | both: %d\n",
            sum(cellExp$byDistance), CLONE_IDENTICAL_CHAINS, sum(cellExp$byIdentical),
            sum(cellExp$byDistance & cellExp$byIdentical)))

saveSource(seqLevel %>% dplyr::select(sequence_id, libid, project, studyGroup, chain,
                                      v_call, j_call, c_call, junction, dist_nearest,
                                      nCellsIdentical, critDistance, critIdentical, expandedSeq),
           "SupplFig5D_sequence_level", "one row per cell per chain, with distances")
```

## The panel

```{r fig_S5D, fig.width=4.6, fig.height=4.2}
s5d <- cellExp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyGroup, project, donorId) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nCellsAssessed = dplyr::n(), nExpandedCells = sum(expanded),
                   propExpanded = mean(expanded), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(project = factor(project, levels = donorLevels)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(project)

s5dP <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(propExpanded ~ studyGroup, data = s5d)$p.value)

pS5D <- ggplot(s5d, aes(studyGroup, propExpanded, colour = studyGroup)) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.45, colour = "black",
               fatten = 1, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, size = 2.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "proportion of expanded cells",
       title = "Supplemental Figure S5D: clonal expansion",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s chain, threshold %.3f | Wilcoxon p = %s",
                          CLONE_CHAINS, CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD, signif(s5dP, 3))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(pS5D)

kable(s5d, caption = "Source data, Supplemental Figure S5D (per donor)")
```

## Sensitivity to the analysis choices

```{r clone_sensitivity}
variants <- list(
  list(label = "heavy chain, threshold 0.193 (reported)",  t = 0.193, ch = "heavy", ident = "heavy"),
  list(label = "heavy distance + identity either chain",   t = 0.193, ch = "heavy", ident = "any"),
  list(label = "any chain, threshold 0.193",               t = 0.193, ch = "any",   ident = "any"),
  list(label = "heavy chain, threshold 0.045",             t = 0.045, ch = "heavy", ident = "heavy"),
  list(label = "heavy chain, identical CDR3 only",         t = 0,     ch = "heavy", ident = "heavy"))

sensitivity <- do.call(rbind, lapply(variants, function(v) {
  e <- callExpansion(dist_threshold = v$t, chains = v$ch, identicalChains = v$ident)
  props <- e$cells %>% dplyr::group_by(project, studyGroup) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(prop = mean(expanded), .groups = "drop")
  data.frame(variant = v$label, cellsAssessed = nrow(e$cells),
             expandedCells = sum(e$cells$expanded),
             pctExpanded = round(100 * mean(e$cells$expanded), 1),
             medianTC = round(median(props$prop[props$studyGroup == "TC"]), 3),
             medianDS = round(median(props$prop[props$studyGroup == "DS"]), 3),
             wilcoxP = round(suppressWarnings(
               tryCatch(wilcox.test(prop ~ studyGroup, data = props)$p.value,
                        error = function(e) NA_real_)), 3))
}))
kable(sensitivity, caption = "Effect of the analysis choices on Supplemental Figure S5D")
saveSource(sensitivity, "SupplFig5D_sensitivity", "sensitivity of the panel to analysis choices")
```

The conclusion --- no significant difference between groups --- holds under every
variant. Two choices are worth stating explicitly in the legend:

- **Chain.** Restricting to the heavy chain is what makes "expanded" mean
  clonally related. Admitting light-chain matches raises apparent expansion
  several-fold, but inspection of the cells it adds shows they carry unrelated
  heavy chains and share only a public kappa rearrangement (IGKV4-1 or IGKV1-39
  with a short stereotyped junction), so they are convergent, not clonal.
- **Threshold.** 0.193 is the value in the methods. `findThreshold()` on these
  data returns a similar value by the gmm method (the density method does not
  converge here), so it is well supported; the gmm fit is stochastic and `SEED`
  fixes it.

```{r clone_carry_forward}
## Carry the expansion calls onto the cell metadata for later steps.
cells <- cells %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cellExp %>% dplyr::select(libid, expanded), by = "libid") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(expanded = tidyr::replace_na(expanded, FALSE))
```

# Repertoire metrics beyond expansion (reviewer comment 8)

Diversity, evenness, dominant-group representation and further repertoire
summary statistics, on the 650 heavy chains of the analysis cells.

**Terminology.** These groups are called *expansion groups*, not clones. A group
is a set of heavy chains that cluster together at the threshold used for
Supplemental Figure S5D; at a length-normalized Hamming distance of 0.193 a
typical CDR3 admits several mismatches, so membership indicates sequence
similarity rather than a verified clonal lineage. Groups of two or more cells are
what the panel counts as expanded.

## Assigning expansion groups

Expansion above was called per sequence from nearest-neighbour distances.
Diversity metrics need group memberships, so sequences are clustered by
**single linkage at the same threshold, within donor x V gene x J gene x
junction-length groups** --- the same grouping `distToNearest` uses.

```{r clone_clustering}
heavyRep <- cloneDist %>%
  dplyr::filter(chain == "heavy") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(jlen = nchar(junction),
                grp  = paste(project, v_call, j_call, jlen, sep = "|"))

assignExpansionGroups <- function(d, threshold = CLONE_DIST_THRESHOLD) {
  if (nrow(d) == 1) return(paste0(d$grp[1], "_1"))
  m <- stringdist::stringdistmatrix(d$junction, d$junction, method = "hamming") / d$jlen[1]
  paste0(d$grp[1], "_", cutree(hclust(as.dist(m), method = "single"), h = threshold))
}

heavyRep <- heavyRep %>%
  dplyr::group_split(grp) %>%
  lapply(function(d) { d$group_id <- assignExpansionGroups(d); d }) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(project, group_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(groupSize = dplyr::n()) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

cat(sprintf("%d heavy chains -> %d expansion groups | largest group %d cells | %d cells in groups of >= 2\n",
            nrow(heavyRep), dplyr::n_distinct(heavyRep$group_id),
            max(heavyRep$groupSize), sum(heavyRep$groupSize >= 2)))
## Audit trail: every multi-cell expansion group with its members.
expandedGroups <- heavyRep %>%
  dplyr::filter(groupSize >= 2) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(project, studyGroup, group_id, groupSize) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(v_gene = paste(unique(v_call), collapse = ";"),
                   j_gene = paste(unique(j_call), collapse = ";"),
                   isotypes = paste(sort(unique(c_call)), collapse = ";"),
                   cdr3_aa = paste(unique(cdr3_aa), collapse = " / "),
                   libids = paste(sort(libid), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(groupSize), project)
kable(expandedGroups %>% dplyr::select(-group_id), caption = "Every multi-cell expansion group")
saveSource(expandedGroups, "Repertoire_expanded_groups", "one row per multi-cell expansion group")

kable(heavyRep %>% dplyr::distinct(project, group_id, groupSize) %>%
        dplyr::count(groupSize, name = "nGroups"),
      caption = "Expansion group size distribution, both groups pooled")
```

Note this yields slightly more cells in expanded groups than the S5D panel
(26 vs 24). The difference is deliberate: criterion (ii) of the published
methods requires a matching **C gene**, whereas the clustering ignores it, since
isotype switching within a lineage is expected biology.

## Per-donor repertoire summary statistics

```{r repertoire_metrics}
hillNumber <- function(p, q) {
  p <- p[p > 0]
  if (q == 1) exp(-sum(p * log(p))) else sum(p^q)^(1 / (1 - q))
}
## Rarefied metrics: resample every donor to a common depth so that diversity is
## not simply a readout of how many cells were sequenced.
rarefy <- function(sizes, n, reps = RAREFY_REPS) {
  pool <- rep(seq_along(sizes), sizes)
  if (length(pool) < n) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  rowMeans(replicate(reps, {
    tab <- table(sample(pool, n)) / n
    c(length(tab), hillNumber(as.numeric(tab), 1))
  }))
}
rarefyDepth <- min(table(heavyRep$project))

repMetrics <- heavyRep %>%
  dplyr::group_split(project) %>%
  lapply(function(d) {
    sizes <- as.numeric(table(d$group_id)); prop <- sizes / sum(sizes)
    rr    <- rarefy(sizes, rarefyDepth)
    vProp <- as.numeric(table(d$v_call)); vProp <- vProp / sum(vProp)
    tibble::tibble(
      project = d$project[1], studyGroup = d$studyGroup[1],
      nCells = nrow(d), nGroups = length(sizes), maxGroupSize = max(sizes),
      pctCellsInExpandedGroups = 100 * sum(sizes[sizes >= 2]) / sum(sizes),
      pctSingletonGroups = 100 * mean(sizes == 1),
      shannon = -sum(prop * log(prop)),
      hill1 = hillNumber(prop, 1), hill2 = hillNumber(prop, 2),
      evenness = -sum(prop * log(prop)) / log(length(sizes)),
      top1Share = 100 * max(sizes) / sum(sizes),
      top5Share = 100 * sum(sort(sizes, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(5, length(sizes)))]) / sum(sizes),
      rarefiedRichness = rr[1], rarefiedHill1 = rr[2],
      vGeneRichness = dplyr::n_distinct(d$v_call),
      vGeneShannon = -sum(vProp * log(vProp)),
      medianCDR3nt = median(d$jlen))
  }) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(project = factor(project, levels = donorLevels)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(project)

cat(sprintf("rarefaction depth = %d cells (the smallest donor)\n", rarefyDepth))
kable(repMetrics %>%
        dplyr::select(project, studyGroup, nCells, nGroups, maxGroupSize,
                      dplyr::all_of(REPORT_METRICS)) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))),
      caption = "Per-donor repertoire metrics (nCells / nGroups / maxGroupSize are context, not tested)")
saveSource(repMetrics %>% dplyr::mutate(project = as.character(project)),
           "Repertoire_metrics_per_donor", "one row per donor, all metrics computed")
```

```{r repertoire_stats}
## Donor-level Wilcoxon on exactly the metrics the figure shows, BH-corrected
## across the six. The corWithDepth column asks whether a metric is really just
## reporting how many cells were sequenced.
repStats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(REPORT_METRICS, function(m) {
  x <- repMetrics[[m]][repMetrics$studyGroup == "TC"]
  y <- repMetrics[[m]][repMetrics$studyGroup == "DS"]
  tibble::tibble(metric = m, medianTC = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 medianDS = median(y, na.rm = TRUE),
                 p = suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x, y)$p.value),
                 corWithDepth = if (m == "nCells") NA_real_ else
                   cor(repMetrics$nCells, repMetrics[[m]], use = "complete.obs"))
})) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(padj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p)

kable(repStats %>% dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))),
      caption = "DS vs Ctrl for the reported metrics (Wilcoxon, BH-corrected across the six), with each metric's correlation with cells sequenced")
saveSource(repStats, "Repertoire_statistics", "one row per reported metric")
```

## Rarefaction: is the repertoire sampled deeply enough to say anything?

```{r fig_rarefaction, fig.width=5.6, fig.height=4}
rarefactionCurve <- heavyRep %>%
  dplyr::group_split(project) %>%
  lapply(function(d) {
    sizes <- as.numeric(table(d$group_id)); pool <- rep(seq_along(sizes), sizes)
    depths <- unique(pmax(1, round(seq(1, length(pool), length.out = 20))))
    tibble::tibble(project = d$project[1], studyGroup = d$studyGroup[1], depth = depths,
                   groups = vapply(depths, function(n)
                     mean(replicate(50, length(unique(sample(pool, n))))), numeric(1)))
  }) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()

pRare <- ggplot(rarefactionCurve, aes(depth, groups, group = project, colour = studyGroup)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS) +
  labs(x = "heavy chains sampled", y = "distinct expansion groups observed", colour = NULL,
       title = "Rarefaction by donor",
       subtitle = "dotted line = one group per cell; curves sit on it, so sampling is the limit") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(pRare)
savePanel(pRare, "Repertoire_rarefaction", width = 5.6, height = 4)
saveSource(rarefactionCurve, "Repertoire_rarefaction", "mean groups observed per sampling depth per donor")
```

## Hill diversity spectrum

```{r fig_hill, fig.width=5.6, fig.height=4}
## alakazam downsamples both groups to a common depth and bootstraps CIs.
divCurve <- alakazam::alphaDiversity(as.data.frame(heavyRep), group = "studyGroup",
                                    clone = "group_id", min_q = 0, max_q = 4,
                                    step_q = 0.25, nboot = DIVERSITY_NBOOT)
divDf <- divCurve@diversity

pHill <- ggplot(divDf, aes(q, d, colour = studyGroup, fill = studyGroup)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = d_lower, ymax = d_upper), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS) +
  labs(x = "diversity order q", y = expression(""^q * D), colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Hill diversity spectrum",
       subtitle = "q=0 richness, q=1 Shannon, q=2 Simpson; shaded = bootstrap 95% CI") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(pHill)
savePanel(pHill, "Repertoire_hill_diversity", width = 5.6, height = 4)
saveSource(divDf, "Repertoire_hill_diversity", "Hill diversity with bootstrap CI by group")
```

# Where this goes next

**Step 3** adds draw-to-processing time, normalizes for visualization, and looks
at cell-level structure (PCA / UMAP). **Step 4** pseudobulks by donor x isotype
and runs the differential expression with
`~ studyGroup + TimeElapsed_binary`.

Isotype is assigned from the heavy chain throughout, so the IgG and IgM subsets
carried into step 4 are the ones in the table above.
